summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Focus on debugging flows for model regressions and latency spikes. Discussed security requirements, dedicated vs hosted routing, and next steps for a short POC.
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-07-14
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jason (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Lena (Product), Maya (Atlas Platform), Omar (CTO), Sara (SRE), Ben (Security), Priyanka (Product)

[00:00] Jason: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jason from Redwood, with Priya and Marco, we'll do a quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis and request logs.
[00:18] Omar: Great thanks, yeah we just want to see how your tooling helps debug model regressions and latency spikes.
[00:25] Priya: Awesome, we'll start with tracing, then error analysis, then show request logs, and end with a quick Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:33] Maya: Sounds good. we're particularly interested in SLOs and how to triage tail latency.
[00:40] Priya: Cool. Opening the console. So on the left nav you'll see Traces -> Error Analysis -> Request Logs -> Rollouts. I'll load a sample app we onboarded earlier.
[01:05] Marco: (screen) here's the traces dashboard, by default we show p50/p95/p99 latency over time and per-route breakdown. You can filter by model, route, client id. Note: our demo data sometimes has artifacts where model names are off — you'll see "redwod-infer" in some traces, transcription and configs, small spelling errors in logs.
[01:30] Sara: That's fine. How are traces captured? Is it agent-side or SDK?
[01:38] Priya: Good q. Tracing is automatic for requests via our SDK or API proxy; we sample heavy requests at higher freq for KV-cache warms and also do continuous tail-sampling. You can configure sampling by route/priority.
[01:55] Ben: Does Elasticsearch house logs or do you use a managed store? Any residency concerns?
[02:02] Jason: Important point. For hosted customers logs are stored in our encrypted managed store; for Private/VPC customers logs stay in their VPC or can be shipped to their SIEM. We support KMS/HSM integration for key management.
[02:20] Ben: Ok, that's helpful.
[02:28] [02:28] Priya: Jumping into a trace example — this is a p99 request that had a 3.2s tail latency. Trace waterfall shows model dispatch, kv cache miss, batch queue wait, and then model inference time. See the spike around the batch queue.
[02:48] Maya: The waterfall looks useful — can we tie that to inflight queue sizes or GPU metrics?
[02:55] Marco: Yes, each trace links to infrastructure metrics. You can open the debug panel and see GPU util, queue length, and other telemetry for the same time window.
[03:10] Omar: If it's a dedicated pool vs hosted, does routing change and how are fallbacks handled?
[03:18] Priya: We have smart routing rules. If dedicated pool is saturated, you can allow overflow to hosted variants or lower-precision quantized models with configurable policy. All of that is visible in the trace metadata.
[03:35] [03:35] Jason: Quick interruption — folks, we sometimes abbreviate Dedicated as "ded" in internal logs, so you'll see ded-pool ids; apologies for the odd labels.
[03:48] Sara: Noted. Can we filter traces by error type? e.g., bad responses vs timeouts vs model hallucinations?
[03:56] Priya: Yes. Error Analysis groups traces by error signatures. You can tag them by similarity — e.g., malformed json outputs, function call mismatches, timeouts, tokenization issues.
[04:12] [04:12] Marco: here's an error cluster view. It shows example transcripts for each error and frequency over time. You can click into a cluster to see raw request/response and the prompt.
[04:27] Maya: Are prompts redacted automatically for pii? we can't leak patient PHI.
[04:34] Jason: For hosted customers we have redaction configs and retention policies; for Private you control retention and redaction. We also integrate with DLP tooling for on-send filtering.
[04:48] Ben: Does Redwood persist full request bodies by default?
[04:53] Priya: Default is to retain request logs for 30 days with redaction enabled for known pii patterns; retention configurable to customer policy and can be turned off.
[05:05] [05:05] Priya: Back to the trace demo — clicking a problematic trace shows per-step metadata. Notice the request had an unexpected function-call shape causing a downstream validation error. We surface the stack trace with the line where the schema mismatch occurred.
[05:25] Omar: Hmm that stack trace — is that coming from customer's code or model runtime?
[05:30] Marco: It's assembled from both. We instrument the SDK to surface client-side errors and the inference runtime for server-side errors. We try to correlate them in a single timeline.
[05:42] Sara: Nice. For debugging is there an easy way to re-run a single trace payload?
[05:47] Priya: Yes, there's a "replay" button. You can replay to a sandbox model version — replay respects sampling and will not affect production unless you explicitly route it.
[05:57] Maya: Good. That helps reproduce nondeterministic behavior.
[06:02] [06:02] Marco: Now switching to Request Logs — this is a searchable store of raw requests/responses. You can run queries by request_id, route, or client_id. We also have quick filters for error codes and latency buckets.
[06:22] Jason: People often want bulk exports for offline analysis. We support CSV/NDJSON exports and direct S3 exports for Private customers.
[06:30] Priyanka (Atlas): If we export logs to S3, can we keep them in our own account?
[06:34] Priya (Redwood): Yes, for Private customers we can configure export to your account; for hosted we offer a managed export with encryption.
[06:44] [06:44] Sara: How long does an export job take? If we request a 7-day window with 100M requests, what's realistic?
[06:52] Marco: It depends on size; for large volumes we spin up a job that can take hours, but for typical POC windows it's under 30 minutes. We'll send a sizing guide.
[07:03] [07:03] Jason: Quick question from the product side — Priya, can you show error regression alerts?
[07:08] Priya: Sure. Under Error Analysis there's an Alerts tab. We can configure alerts on error clusters, regression vs a baseline prompt set, or sudden p95 jumps. Alerts integrate with Slack, PagerDuty, and email.
[07:22] Omar: Can alerts be tied to a specific prompt test? e.g., if a prompt set fails quality threshold then trigger rollback?
[07:28] Priya: Yes. We have Eval-linked alerts. You can create a prompt set baseline and if quality metric drops > X% we can trigger a canary rollback or notify the team.
[07:42] [07:42] Maya: That rollback — is it automatic or manual?
[07:45] Marco: Configurable. You can set automatic rollback policies for model revs or route fallbacks, but we recommend canary + human approval for major changes.
[07:56] Ben: For audit, do rollbacks and alerts produce audit logs?
[08:00] Jason: Yes, all actions are auditable in the Console's Activity log with user, timestamp, and change details.
[08:10] [08:10] Priya: Now we'll demonstrate a debugging flow: user reports hallucination spike. We filter traces for that time range and error type. We then pivot to request logs and pull sample prompts. From there we can check model version, quantization profile, and routing policy at that time.
[08:33] Priyanka (Atlas): Can we compare two time windows side by side? Say last week vs this week?
[08:38] Marco: Yes, there's a compare view — you can pick two ranges and overlay p95/p99 and error clusters.
[08:47] Sara: Are there integrations with Sentry or our internal tracing system?
[08:51] Priya: We provide webhooks and export connectors. For deep integration we can push trace metadata to your tracing backend.
[08:59] [08:59] Omar: One of our constraints is HIPAA compliance. Can you confirm private deployment options and where logs live?
[09:06] Jason: For HIPAA we recommend Private (VPC) deployments with customer-managed KMS. In that mode logs and traces never leave your network unless you configure exports. We can provide BAA and compliance docs.
[09:20] Ben: We'll need SOC2 + BAA copy.
[09:23] Jason: We'll send that in the follow-up.
[09:30] [09:30] Priya: Now quick demo of Request Logs filters. I'm filtering by error code 502 and p99>1s. You can jump from the list into trace view and from there to infra metrics.
[09:48] Maya: Do you keep model input tokens in logs or do you store only metadata by default?
[09:53] Marco: By default we store sanitized inputs and an abbreviated transcript. Full inputs are optional and gated by redaction policies.
[10:03] [10:03] Priya: Showing the live debug panel — you can attach notes, assign to a user, and create an action directly from a trace. That action will create a ticket in Jira if you wire the integration.
[10:18] Priyanka (Atlas): Great. For our internal process we'd like auto-created tickets for any p99 > 2s on critical routes.
[10:24] Priya: That is doable — we'll add it to the alert rule in the POC config.
[10:30] [10:30] Marco: A note about sampling: heavy sampling for tail requests increases storage. For POC we'll recommend targeted sampling on critical routes plus higher retention just for the trial.
[10:46] Sara: For the POC are there any rate limits or quotas we should know about?
[10:51] Jason: POC sandboxes have standard quotas; we'll provide a temporary bump for the pilot traffic. We'll include that in the checklist.
[10:59] [10:59] Omar: Are there any gotchas around replay that could cause stateful side effects? e.g., downstream webhooks firing?
[11:06] Priya: Replays are sandboxed by default and we mask downstream integrations; but if you choose to run replays against your staging endpoints you need to opt in.
[11:18] [11:18] Priyanka (Atlas): On routing: is it possible to route only certain customers to Dedicated while others stay hosted?
[11:24] Marco: Yes, routing is per-tenant or per-route. You can pin client ids to a dedicated pool and have fallback policies.
[11:34] Maya: How do you handle model versioning in traces? can we see which model/tensor quant was used?
[11:40] Priya: Every trace includes model id, model version, quantization profile, and the kernel/exec path. That makes it easier to correlate regressions with quantization changes.
[11:52] [11:52] Jason: Quick demo of Error Analysis drilldown: we find a cluster where the output format changed after a model update. You can see the rollout history and which clients were affected.
[12:08] Ben: Can we restrict which engineers can trigger rollbacks?
[12:12] Priya: Yes, RBAC supports per-action permissions. Also SSO/SAML integration is supported and logged.
[12:22] [12:22] Marco: On observability — Console exposes per-route cost breakdowns by token and infra. That helps evaluate tradeoffs between longer context windows vs latency/cost.
[12:36] Maya: Are there built-in recommendations for batching and quantization?
[12:40] Priya: That's part of Redwood Optimize but Console surfaces suggested batching and a recommended quant profile per workload.
[12:49] [12:49] Jason: We're about half-way — any burning questions?
[12:53] Omar: One: can we run a controlled canary where 5% of requests go to a new model and we collect traces only for those?
[12:59] Priya: Yes, canary + trace sampling is a standard pattern.
[13:05] [13:05] Marco: Next, demo of request log export. I'll run a quick NDJSON export of a 3-hour window and show the format. You can see request_id, client_id, route, model_id, duration_ms, error_code, and a redacted prompt.
[13:25] Priyanka (Atlas): For privacy we need to ensure PHI fields are masked at ingestion, is there an API hook?
[13:31] Priya: There's an ingestion webhook where you can plug in a DLP step pre-ingest, or we can ship a redaction lambda to run in your VPC for Private customers.
[13:45] [13:45] Sara: Around retention policies, can we set per-route retention? e.g., test routes vs prod?
[13:51] Marco: Yes, retention is per-route and can be overridden.
[13:56] [13:56] Jason: Quick recap of the debugging flow: trace -> inspect waterfall -> pivot to request logs -> replay -> adjust routing/rollout or rollback. We'll capture actions as tickets.
[14:10] Maya: Helpful. We'll want to see the exact POC config.
[14:14] Jason: We'll send the POC checklist and a recommended sampling/retention config.
[14:21] [14:21] Priya: Last topic — permissions and audit. I'll show the Activity log. Every trace view, rollback, or export shows who did it.
[14:34] Ben: We'll verify that against our compliance needs.
[14:38] [14:38] Marco: Quick live Q&A — Omar?
[14:40] Omar: Are there any latency overheads from tracing? e.g., does instrumentation add 10-20ms?
[14:46] Priya: Very minor. SDK instrumentation adds low single-digit ms typically. Heavy sampling and large trace payloads can add overhead but we keep that minimal by async shipping and batching.
[14:59] [14:59] Maya: For the POC traffic is our data encrypted at rest?
[15:03] Jason: Yes, at rest and in transit. For Private we support customer-managed keys.
[15:10] [15:10] Priya: Wrapping up — we'll do follow-ups: send security pack (SOC2/ISO/BAA), pricing and Dedicated options, POC checklist, and sandbox invites.
[15:22] Jason: Thanks all. Any final questions?
[15:25] Priyanka (Atlas): Not from me. We'll coordinate on sample traces and SLOs.
[15:29] Omar: No, thanks. Looks good.
[15:32] Jason: Great. We'll follow up with the items discussed. Thanks everyone.

(Transcript end — exported from Fireflies, minor transcription artifacts present)
